court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Vaibhav Vinod Goyal And 8 Others vs State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Ps Khadan Akola And ...

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Vaibhav Vinod Goyal, Usha Vinod Goyal, Hina Achal Agrawal, Anchal Agrawal, Shikha Manish Singhal, Manish Singhal, Rekha Govind Singhal, Govind Singhal, Anil Tambi
parties.respondent_defendant: State of Maharashtra, Pooja Vaibhav Goyal

facts_of_case: The applicants are challenging the registration of a first information report filed against them for the offence punishable under Sections 498-A, 504, 506 read with Section 109 IPC.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the applicant to prove that the FIR is not maintainable.
legal_principles.held: We have carefully considered the allegations in the first information report and we are satisfied that even if the allegations in the first information report along with the material on record are taken on its face value, the same are not sufficient to constitute the essential ingredients of the offences alleged.

legal_principles.principle: A joint petition for mutual divorce filed under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act can be a ground to quash and set aside an FIR.
legal_principles.held: They have filed a joint petition under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act before the Family Court at Akola. A copy of the said joint petition is placed on record by the applicants at Annexure-A2.

outcome.final_order: Rule is made returnable forthwith. Heard finally by consent of the parties.
